body:
## Problem

- An operator cannot cancel a running workflow. The row Cancel action and a direct API call both fail with a validation error, and the run keeps going.
- The CDP cancel route checks each id with a version-aware UUID rule.
- The invocation store issues UUIDTs, which carry no RFC version. The rule rejects every id the runs list shows.
- The failure is new. It arrived with invocation cancellation and affects every caller of the by-id selector.

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a07d26-4ee8-78e2-a40c-9bfee53592d5 -->
## Origin

- Replay Vision
- Conversations: [ticket 1](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a0c2a5-0cfe-0000-1ef6-edf3b83a5460), [ticket 2](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a0ceed-3fc4-0000-b784-d356347d13a4)
- Scout: a custom scout
- First signal: 2026-09-07
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a07d26-4ee8-78e2-a40c-9bfee53592d5)
- Likely cause: [`5a67b89`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/5a67b89b4724b69a9f710ca0bb32a8d547639f79)
- Task started by: a person, from the inbox
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a07d26-4ee8-78e2-a40c-9bfee53592d5 -->

## Changes

- Cancel now accepts the ids the runs list shows, so the Cancel button and the API both stop runs.
- The route matches the `8-4-4-4-12` shape with `UUID.validateString`, the helper that already ignores RFC versions for the same reason.
- A malformed id still returns 400. That is the point of the check: it keeps the value away from the `::uuid[]` bind in `cancelJobs`.
- Nothing user-visible changes beyond the button working. No UI code is touched, so there is no screenshot to show.

## How did you test this code?

Two test groups, each aimed at a regression no existing test caught.

- `cdp-api.serial.test.ts`: every existing cancel test used the `all: true` selector, so the `invocation_ids` path had no coverage at all. The new cases send ids the invocation store issues, and one id that is not UUID-shaped. Removing the fix turns the first case red and leaves the second green.
- `test_hog_flow_cancel.py`: the by-id proxy test used a `uuid4`, which passes either rule. It now runs as a parameterized pair over an issued id and an RFC uuid, so a version-aware check added to the Django serializer would fail here.

<details>
<summary>Local runs</summary>

- `jest --config jest.serial.config.js --testPathPatterns=cdp-api.serial -t cancel` — 18 passed.
- `pytest products/workflows/backend/api/test/test_hog_flow_cancel.py` — 18 passed.
- Confirmed the bug first: with the fix reverted, the new node case fails.

Not checked: the fix was not exercised against a live cyclotron queue, only against a stubbed `cancelJobs`.

</details>

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None. No user-facing documentation describes the id format.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

Written by Claude Code from a PostHog inbox report. Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/simplify`.

The report named three possible causes: the UI sending no id, a strict validation rule, and missing API coverage. Only the second holds. The UI already passes `row.invocation_id`, and Django's `UUIDField` accepts a UUIDT, so both observed errors came from the same zod rule on the CDP route. Confirmed by generating UUIDTs against zod 4's `.uuid()` in isolation: it rejected all 200.

`nodejs/src/cdp/schema/hogflow.ts` applies the same version-aware rule to `message_category_id` and `template_uuid`, which are also UUIDT-backed. That is a separate surface and is left alone here.

No duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "invocation_ids cancel"` found nothing.

Public artifact: the diff, the commit message, and this description contain no material from the agent session. The test ids are generated at run time.

title: fix(workflows): accept issued invocation ids when cancelling runs
